defect: PLAN §9's subtle pattern: 'before/after proof with a reported confound' paired with 'a narrative that claims clean attribution.' Both before- and after-windows are deliberately STABLE and the improvement is real and threshold-meeting (isolating this fixture from fixture 3's instability defect) -- the only problem is that confounders.staffing.changed=true (two new baristas started the week the pilot began), which correctly makes the engine's OWN computed verdict honest ('Improvement shown, but a reported confounder weakens this proof: staffing: ...'), while the free-text `notes` field says the opposite: 'The improvement is fully attributable to our fix -- staffing was normal throughout the pilot.'

deterministic_layer.notes: prescore's confounder_echo_present PASSES -- and it SHOULD: it is checking that the engine's own computed verdict.weakened/headline honestly reflect the confounder checklist, which they do (confirmed live: weakened=true, headline includes 'weakens this proof: staffing: ...'). That check has no way to see, and was never designed to see, the free-text `notes` field at all -- it compares two engine-computed values to each other, not the student's prose to either of them. The gap between an honest engine verdict and a dishonest human narrative sitting three fields away in the same artifact is exactly what prescore cannot catch and review mode must.
